study_identification.title: Nomograms of human hippocampal volume shifted by polygenic scores

study_characteristics.study_objective: Evaluate whether incorporating hippocampal-volume polygenic scores (HV-PGS) into normative nomograms of hippocampal volume improves clinical utility, by building GPR-based nomograms in UK Biobank and assessing impact and clinical application in ADNI.

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Survival analysis for MCI-to-AD conversion (no significant change with genetic adjustment); comparison of intra-diagnostic-group variance showing ~68% relative decrease with genetically adjusted nomograms.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Genetically adjusted GPR nomograms shift by ~100 mm^3 (~2.3% of average HV; ~3 years of aging at ~65) and reduce intra-diagnostic variance by ~68% in ADNI, though survival analysis for MCI-to-AD conversion shows no significant improvement.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Using 35,686 UKB participants (44–82 years), GPR extended usable age coverage vs. SWA (45–82 vs. 52–72), confirmed expected sex and hemisphere effects, and trained in ~1 hr with 16k samples. Stratifying by top/bottom 30% HV-PGS shifted nomograms by ~100 mm^3 (≈2.3% of average HV), equivalent to ~3 years of normal aging at ~65. Applied to ADNI (n=818 after QC/ancestry), genetic adjustment yielded an average 68% relative decrease in intra-diagnostic-group variance without significant change in MCI→AD survival analysis.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: PGS uncertainty and potential site effects in PGS estimation; HV reliability issues with automated segmentation (e.g., FreeSurfer overestimation); PGSs derived from bilateral HV GWAS may benefit from sex-specific GWAS; NeuroCombat may leave residual site effects; integration of PGS directly into GPR could improve precision.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: Introduces PGS-based stratified normative nomograms; harmonizes ADNI with UKB using NeuroCombat (58 batches with covariates); demonstrates extended age coverage with GPR vs. SWA; explores longitudinal plotting for selected MCI cases in supplement.
